content.title: Management of Heart Failure in Adult Congenital Heart Disease (excerpt)
recommendations: Timely evaluation for transplantation by ACHD HF specialists in a transplant centre with ACHD expertise is recommended.
Ventricular assist devices can bridge patients to transplantation, or in a subgroup of patients, may be an option as destination therapy.
ACHD patients with chronic HF should be referred to specialized centres.
Specific guidelines for medical treatment of chronic HF in ACHD are lacking; practitioners should follow current general HF guidelines.
Sacubitril/valsartan may decrease morbidity, but no formal recommendation can be made due to retrospective/anecdotal nature of observations.
Co-morbidities in HF (diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, central sleep apnoea, iron deficiency, cachexia) should be treated according to specific recommendations in the document.

In biventricular circulation, patients with an impaired systemic left ventricle should be treated with conventional HF therapy; similar consideration may apply to symptomatic patients with a failing systemic right ventricle.
Diuretics are recommended to control symptoms of fluid retention.

Treatment of symptomatic patients with a failing single ventricle (e.g., Fontan circulation) or persistent right-to-left shunt should be initiated carefully, taking ventricular preload and systemic afterload into account.

Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) may be a therapeutic option in ACHD patients with HF, but evidence in this setting is still lacking; efficacy depends on structural/functional substrate (ventricle anatomy, AV valve regurgitation, myocardial disease/scarring, type of conduction delay).
Treatment of acute HF in ACHD patients should be in an expert centre with knowledge of inotropes, availability of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and advanced bridging techniques.
content.notes: Recommendations repeated emphasize specialist-centre care and individualized consideration of device therapies. Evidence gaps are noted for several therapies in ACHD-specific HF populations.
